Phase-entry SHA e0ddd482. CLASSIFICATIONS (one primary disposition per finding, model of phase-prompt section 6): V-2 = A (RDGO-001 section 4/6 'Gate 5 creates PROOF_VERIFIED_AND_BOUND over the completed approval digest' is stale; the verified reality -- HPAC-REQ-054 step 10 in hpac_verifier.bind_gate5_canonical creates sequence 3 at Gate 3 time over the HPAC-APPROVAL-SUBJECT/2.0 digest, and Gate 5 confirms it read-only -- is correct and loses no trust property that RDGO section 6 substantively requires; the assurance gate stays at Gate 5 / validate_approval NON-REAL hard stop; no contradiction between contracts). V-3 = A, subsumed by V-2 (RDGO section 4 'over the completed approval digest' is the same stale wording; the bind is over the subject digest; RIASC-001's separate completed-record record_digest is substantively correct and needs only a clarifying cross-reference so the two digests are not conflated). V-4 = A (PBRD-001 section 4 fact 14's 7-field human_authority_binding enumeration is stale relative to the verified 3-field production RuntimeDispatchHumanAuthorityBinding (approval_id, approval_record_digest, validation_evidence_digest); .1R.13 section 10 proved the collapse lossless -- every omitted logical field is direct, or deterministically committed inside validation_evidence_digest = SHA-256 over the 14-key projection payload, or structurally enforced more strongly than a string (exact-object registry membership for the projection identity), or a zero-entropy constant (authority_contract_version); collision analysis re-confirmed: no two contract-distinguishable authority contexts share a 3-tuple binding). V-13-3-1 = D (the contracts are correct -- RDGO section 8 gives Gate 7 the policy version as an input, not a mandate to re-run PB; section 15 places policy re-evaluation with Gate 6; only the .1R.13.2 planning prose 'PB-policy drift covered transitively via projection revalidation' overstates revalidate_validated_authority_projection, which does NOT re-read live PB policy and explicitly tolerates policy_drift_requires_fresh_pb_re_evaluation, returning True; fix = .1R.13.2 doc erratum + one clarifying RDGO section 8 sentence; do NOT add PB re-evaluation to Gate 7; a future scoped phase MAY add policy_version to Gate6Decision but it is not a prerequisite). V-13-3-2 = D (Gate 7's Gate7Result.matched_no_go_ids is a per-decision projection of the design-only authorization/safety flag snapshot (runtime_enforcement_safety_authorization.py, Phase 104C -- 10 flag-mapped ids RE-NOGO-001..008/010/011) and omits registry-mandatory RE-NOGO-009/013/015/016/017; those five are environmental-readiness capability gaps -- audit persistence, telegram inbound, emergency abort, output capture, recovery procedure -- enforced by the separate execution-enablement readiness process (V0_2_EXECUTION_READINESS_NO_GO_GATES.md), not per-decision authorization/safety flags; matched_no_go_ids is diagnostic evidence, never a decision input (Gate 8 .1R.13.5 section 51 and Gate 9 .1R.15 section 29 both verified nothing gates on its completeness; ten independent flag-mapped no-gos already force DENY); fix = annotate docs/RUNTIME_ENFORCEMENT_NO_GO_REGISTRY.md to schema 1.1 classifying each of the 17 entries as per-decision / environmental-readiness / advisory + a scoping sentence; no Gate-7 re-open, no production change). V-13-5-1 = A primary + a class-C secondary note (.1R.13.1 section 11.2/25/26/27 froze gate8_cwd_drift / gate8_environment_allowlist_drift / gate8_transport_drift as anti-substitution DRIFT rows requiring a diff against a bound reference, but RuntimeDispatchRequestConstructionInput carries no bound cwd_ref / env_allowlist_ref / transport_ref -- the frozen plan is internally inconsistent; the verified implementation reasonably realized cwd as a repository-scope containment check, env as a name well-formedness check, transport as the contract-fixed const local_cli with no drift check, and BOUND the cwd/env values into containment_evidence_digest which .1R.15 section 29 proved Gate 9 genuinely recomputes by re-running run_gate8_process_containment and read-back-verifies -- V-13-5-1 CLOSED for the runtime-dispatch consumption path; the effect plan is trusted-coordinator-assembled, never caller input, so there is no caller cwd/env reference to diff; fix = RDGO section 9 three-layer model paragraph (direct validation / canonical digest commitment / Gate-9 recomputation) + strike the transport row + reword the cwd/env rows in a .1R.13.1 erratum; optional non-prerequisite Gate-8 hardening (add cwd_ref/env_allowlist_ref, same pattern as PBRD fact 13 filesystem_scope_ref) = the class-C secondary note for a future hardening slice). V-15-1 = C, HIGHEST PRIORITY (the contracts are internally inconsistent -- .1R.9 section 13.5 says BOTH 'the coordinator acquires [the lock] before the section 12 battery so two racers cannot both pass revalidation and both create' AND 'Do not invent a new lock -- the protected create-only commit is itself the atomic transaction'; RDGO-001 section 10 'revalidates ... while holding the protected evidence-store serialization boundary ... without a TOCTOU allowance' and .1R.13.1 section 16.2 invariant 4 same wording -- AND the verified implementation has a real gap: run_gate9_atomic_authority_consumption runs its revalidation battery (projection re-trust + revalidate_validated_authority_projection which re-runs validate_approval + subject/scope digest + read-only sequence-3 confirm + proof/approval pairing + capability re-read + consumption-record absence check) IMMEDIATELY BEFORE but NOT ATOMIC WITH the create-only atomic primitive write_atomic_create_only (O_EXCL temp sibling + atomic link-if-absent), which is the true linearization point and the only transaction mechanism -- no Lock/flock/advisory-lock object exists in the coordinator or runtime_invocation_authority_consumption.py; between the final revalidation (T1) and the atomic create (T3) the code does only local file reads + hashing + record construction, no sleep/subprocess/network/write-open (test_no_effectful_step_between_last_revalidation_and_create), but a revocation / lifecycle-invalidation / concurrent adversarial write landing in the T1->T3 window is NOT caught (test_v15_1_residual_revalidate_to_create_window), so a canonical HPAC-AUTHORITY-CONSUMPTION/2.0 record can be written for authority that was invalid at T3. INDEPENDENT ANSWER to 'must authority be valid exactly at the consumption linearization point?': YES -- Gate 9 is the atomic one-shot authority-consumption point and RDGO-001 section 10 explicitly disclaims a TOCTOU allowance; a permanent canonical 'consumed' fact must not exist for authority invalid at the instant of the create-only linearization; the verified implementation makes the validity check and the consumption ADJACENT, not ATOMIC -- a real semantic gap. Per phase-prompt section 12 this classifies V-15-1 as REQUIRING A NARROW PRODUCTION REPAIR BEFORE GATE 10 IS DESIGNED. It is nevertheless NON-BLOCKING for Gate-10 planning AUTHORIZATION because: no external effect follows (Gate 10 does not exist, no phase ID, no adapter-dispatch path); the frozen Gate9Result -> Gate-10 forward invariant already re-closes it (is_gate9_result is provenance-only; a future Gate 10 MUST additionally require status == consumed AND re-read consumption.json AND re-validate all mutable authority AND re-establish containment before the first effect); the outcome is fail-safe (a stale-authority record BURNS the one-shot authority, never escalates it, and any retry needs a fresh approval + attempt_id + proof_id anyway); the production path is unreachable (real Gate 7 always DENY, real run_gate5 never returns a Gate5Result); and Gates 5-8 all closed with the identical revalidate-immediately-before-the-atomic-step pattern. SELECTED FIX = Option B (of the phase-prompt section 14 alternatives): capture monotonic authority-generation tokens for each mutable authority source inside the section 12 battery (principal status generation, credential generation, lifecycle-chain head digest, proof lifecycle state, consumption-record absence); immediately before create, re-read ONLY those tokens with ZERO intervening effectful I/O and fail closed on any change; embed the token snapshot into the consumption record's authority_binding so Gate 10's mandatory re-read can also detect a post-consumption change; NO second lock (respects the create-only-primitive-as-transaction rule); optionally combined with Option A (per-proof_id advisory serialization) for same-proof racer hygiene. Option A alone is insufficient (it serializes same-proof Gate-9 racers but not an external revocation actor in a different lock domain); Option C (immutable versioned snapshot) is a fallback that accepts as-of-snapshot semantics; Option D (conditional compare-and-create store primitive) is over-scoped for a narrow repair. V-15-2 = D (test hygiene: .1R.14's V-13-1 extension normalized ten guard suites but missed three HPAC-foundation 'zero-production-consumers' point-in-time guards in the _3w1r2b1r111r31 / _3w1r2b1r111r32 / _3w1r2b1r111r321 suites; they trip on runtime_dispatch_gate9.py's legitimate authorized imports of hpac_foundation / runtime_invocation_authority_consumption / hpac_lifecycle; A/B PASS at c1ea2c8b, FAIL at b618f353; convert to phase-aware SUBSET invariants (consumers - AUTHORIZED_CONSUMERS == set(), AUTHORIZED_CONSUMERS explicitly enumerated incl. runtime_dispatch_gate9 citing .1R.14/.1R.15), keep the HPAC verifier trust-root asserts and the _GATE9_RESULTS owner / Gate-10 zero-consumer asserts EXACT, unauthorized future consumers still fail, no broad silent allowlist; fold into .1R.15.2). V-15-3 = D (test quality: three .1R.14 integration-suite tests (~lines 780/820/865) raw-assign runtime_dispatch_gate5.is_gate5_result = lambda ... instead of monkeypatch.setattr, leaving a stale closure module-installed after the file; switch to monkeypatch.setattr + a post-file restoration assertion; fold into .1R.15.2).
